answer:
Rectangle \(ABCD\) has sides \(\overline{AB}\) of length 4 and \(\overline{BC}\) of length 3. We divide \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) into 168 congruent segments each, resulting in points \(P_k\) on \(\overline{AB}\) and \(Q_k\) on \(\overline{BC}\). Similarly, we divide \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) into 168 congruent segments each, resulting in points \(R_k\) on \(\overline{AD}\) and \(S_k\) on \(\overline{CD}\). For each \(1 \le k \le 167\), we draw segments \(\overline{P_kQ_k}\) and \(\overline{R_kS_k}\), and then draw the diagonal \(\overline{AC}\).

All these segments are parallel to the diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) with slope \(3/4\). The length of each segment \(\overline{P_kQ_k}\) and \(\overline{R_kS_k}\) is proportional to \(5 \times \frac{168 - k}{168}\). 

The sum of the lengths of the segments \(\overline{P_kQ_k}\) for \(1 \le k \le 167\) is calculated as follows:
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{167} \text{length}(\overline{P_kQ_k}) = \frac{5}{168} \sum_{k=1}^{167} (168 - k) = \frac{5}{168} \cdot \frac{167 \cdot 168}{2} = \frac{5 \cdot 167}{2} = 417.5
\]
Similarly, the sum of the lengths of the segments \(\overline{R_kS_k}\) is also 417.5. Adding these sums and the length of the diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) (which is 5) gives:
\[
2 \times 417.5 + 5 = 835 + 5 = 840
\]

Thus, the sum of the lengths of the 335 parallel segments drawn is \(\boxed{840}\).
